description: Same-session secure response editing (design §2). Adds a per-form responseEditing mode (disabled default / timed+minutes / until_close) in schema.settings, a stateless HMAC edit token (node:crypto) returned on submit, a new public CSRF-exempt edit endpoint that re-validates and overwrites the response, and the 'Edit my response' frontend flow. No migration (editedAt lives in metadata JSON; token is stateless). Depends on FEAT-001: it reuses the Vitest runner added there and the editor Settings/save plumbing, and it threads settings through the same getFormSchema/updateFormSettings/getPublicForm paths FEAT-001 extended.
steps: API settings (§2.1): in form.service.ts add `responseEditing?: "disabled"|"timed"|"until_close"` and `responseEditMinutes?: number` to the FormSchema.settings type; in getFormSchema default them to "disabled" and 15 (concrete defaults); in updateFormSettings merge both via per-field conditional spread. In form.schemas.ts add `responseEditing: z.enum(["disabled","timed","until_close"]).optional()` and `responseEditMinutes: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(1440).optional()` to updateFormSettingsSchema. (The web FormSchema.settings fields were already added in FEAT-001.)

Env (§2.3): in apps/api/src/config/env.ts add `RESPONSE_EDIT_SECRET: optional("RESPONSE_EDIT_SECRET", "dev-insecure-response-edit-secret-change-me")` and a boot `console.warn` when NODE_ENV==='production' and the var is unset; document RESPONSE_EDIT_SECRET in .env.example under the API section.

Token service (§2.3): new apps/api/src/services/responseEditToken.ts importing createHmac + timingSafeEqual from node:crypto; `signEditToken(responseId, expiresAt)` → base64url(JSON {rid,exp}) + '.' + base64url(hmacSha256); `verifyEditToken(token)` → { responseId, exp } | null, returning null on malformed input / bad signature (constant-time timingSafeEqual) / JSON parse failure; does NOT check expiry.

Token unit test (§2.10) — SECURITY CORE: new apps/api/src/services/responseEditToken.test.ts (inject a known RESPONSE_EDIT_SECRET via process.env) — sign/verify round-trip; null for tampered payload, bad signature, garbage, truncated token, token with no '.' separator; confirm timingSafeEqual is used.

Extract shared helpers (§2.5 step 6, step 7): in form.service.ts extract `validateSubmission(schema, answers)` containing ONLY the three answer gates (unknown-question rejection, visibility-aware required check incl. MULTI_ENTRY empty-array special-case, per-answer validateAnswerAgainstQuestion loop) — NO email-required, NO duplicate logic; and `computeQuizScore(schema, answers)` from the quiz block (null when quizMode off). Rewire submitFormResponse to call both; keep its EMAIL_REQUIRED/DUPLICATE_RESPONSE gates wrapped around validateSubmission. Export validateSubmission for testing.

validateSubmission unit test (§2.10): new *.test.ts next to form.service.ts asserting validateSubmission throws INVALID_RESPONSE for unknown question id, missing required (incl. MULTI_ENTRY empty array), and type-mismatched answer; passes a valid payload.

Issue token (§2.4, §2.6): in submitFormResponse compute editToken from the mode (disabled→null; timed→now+minutes*60; until_close→min(scheduledCloseAt, now+24h) or now+24h) and return { ...response, quizScore, editToken }; in form.routes.ts submit route add `...(response.editToken ? { editToken: response.editToken } : {})` to the response body.

Edit schema + service (§2.5): in form.schemas.ts `editResponseSchema = submitResponseSchema.extend({ editToken: z.string().min(1).max(2000) })`. In form.service.ts `editFormResponse(slug, responseId, input, editToken)` in order: verify token (null→INVALID_EDIT_TOKEN 403); rid must equal responseId (mismatch→INVALID_EDIT_TOKEN 403 + console.warn); dedicated lookup `status: { in: ["PUBLISHED","CLOSED"] }` (none→PUBLIC_FORM_NOT_FOUND 404); load response scoped by formId (none→RESPONSE_NOT_FOUND 404); re-check mode/window (disabled→EDITING_DISABLED 403; timed expiry via submittedAt+minutes→EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED 403; until_close CLOSED or elapsed scheduledCloseAt→EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED 403 NEVER FORM_CLOSED; token exp upper bound→EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED 403); re-run validateSubmission(schema, answers) only (INVALID_RESPONSE 400); overwrite answers + stamp metadata.editedAt (merge existing metadata); return { id, submittedAt (original, not rewritten), quizScore (recomputed via computeQuizScore) }. No emails, no analytics submission event on edit.

Edit route + app.ts wiring (§2.5, §2.8): in form.routes.ts add public route `POST /public/:slug/responses/:responseId/edit` parsing editResponseSchema, passing req.body.editToken (post-validation, never from query/header) to editFormResponse, returning { response: { id, submittedAt }, quizScore? }. In app.ts add three 403 cases to the switch: INVALID_EDIT_TOKEN, EDITING_DISABLED, EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED (PUBLIC_FORM_NOT_FOUND/RESPONSE_NOT_FOUND/INVALID_RESPONSE already mapped; FORM_CLOSED deliberately unused here).

Editor Settings controls (§2.1): in FormEditorPage.tsx add responseEditing/responseEditMinutes state loaded from schema.settings, a Settings-tab control (mode select + minutes input shown only when 'timed'), and include both in the saveFormSettings PATCH body.

PublicFormPage edit flow (§2.7): add same-session state responseId/editToken/editWindowExpiresAt/isEditing; on submit success capture response.id + editToken and compute the client window end (timed→submittedAt+minutes*60000; until_close→scheduledCloseAt or null); on the confirmation screen show an 'Edit my response' button + note when a token exists and not client-expired; clicking sets isEditing, clears submitted, re-renders prefilled from in-memory answers; branch handleSubmit to POST the edit endpoint when editing (answers, email when collected, metadata, editToken), on success return to confirmation keeping the same token; setInterval/timeout hides the button at expiry (UX only); map 403 EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED/EDITING_DISABLED/INVALID_EDIT_TOKEN to the design's user messages.
acceptance_criteria: `cd apps/api && pnpm test` passes including responseEditToken.test.ts and the validateSubmission test.
`cd apps/api && pnpm exec tsc --project tsconfig.json --noEmit` exits 0.
`cd apps/web && pnpm exec tsc -b --noEmit` exits 0 and `cd apps/web && pnpm test` passes.

A disabled form issues no editToken and rejects edits; a timed form returns a token on submit and an edit overwrites answers + sets metadata.editedAt without a new submission event or emails; a responseId-mismatched token returns 403 INVALID_EDIT_TOKEN; a CLOSED until_close form returns 403 EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED (not 410).
verification: cd apps/api && pnpm exec tsc --project tsconfig.json --noEmit && pnpm test
cd apps/web && pnpm exec tsc -b --noEmit && pnpm test
Run the feasible items of design §2.11 manual checklist against a dev server + published test form
findings:
DONE. API tsc 0 + 21 tests pass (8 responseEditToken + 8 FEAT-001 schema + 5 validateSubmission); web tsc -b 0 + 25 tests pass. No Prisma migration. No deviation from the design.

API changes (apps/api):
- form.service.ts: added responseEditing/responseEditMinutes to the FormSchema.settings type; getFormSchema defaults them to "disabled"/15 (concrete defaults — downstream never branches on undefined); updateFormSettings merges both via per-field conditional spread. Imported signEditToken/verifyEditToken from ../../services/responseEditToken.js.
- Extracted THREE shared helpers near isAnswerCorrect: isQuestionVisibleFor(question, answers) (lifted the submit closure to take answers explicitly), validateSubmission(schema, answers) EXPORTED (the pinned 3-gate boundary: unknown-question, visibility-aware required incl. MULTI_ENTRY empty-array, per-answer validateAnswerAgainstQuestion loop — NO email, NO duplicate), and computeQuizScore(schema, answers) (null when quizMode off). submitFormResponse now calls validateSubmission (EMAIL_REQUIRED/DUPLICATE still wrapped around it) + computeQuizScore, and returns { ...response, quizScore, editToken } where editToken comes from new computeEditToken(schema, responseId) (disabled->null; timed->now+minutes*60000; until_close->min(scheduledCloseAt, now+UNTIL_CLOSE_CAP_MS=24h) or now+24h).
- NEW editFormResponse(slug, responseId, input, editToken): verify token (null->INVALID_EDIT_TOKEN 403), rid!==responseId->INVALID_EDIT_TOKEN 403 + console.warn, dedicated lookup status in [PUBLISHED,CLOSED] (none->PUBLIC_FORM_NOT_FOUND 404), response scoped by formId (none->RESPONSE_NOT_FOUND 404), live mode/window recheck (disabled->EDITING_DISABLED 403; timed via submittedAt+minutes->EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED 403; until_close CLOSED or elapsed scheduledCloseAt->EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED 403 NEVER FORM_CLOSED; token exp upper bound->EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED 403), validateSubmission only, overwrite answers + merge metadata.editedAt (ISO), returns { id, submittedAt (original, select-only), quizScore (recomputed) }. No emails/analytics on edit.
- NEW apps/api/src/services/responseEditToken.ts: createHmac+timingSafeEqual from node:crypto; getSecret() reads process.env.RESPONSE_EDIT_SECRET LAZILY (so the test can inject before import); signEditToken/verifyEditToken (base64url payload{rid,exp}.base64url(hmac)); verify returns null on malformed/bad-sig (length-guarded timingSafeEqual)/parse fail; does NOT check expiry.
- form.schemas.ts: added responseEditing z.enum + responseEditMinutes z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(1440) to updateFormSettingsSchema; NEW editResponseSchema = submitResponseSchema.extend({ editToken: z.string().min(1).max(2000) }).
- form.routes.ts: submit route body now spreads ...(response.editToken ? { editToken } : {}); NEW public route POST /public/:slug/responses/:responseId/edit parses editResponseSchema and passes input.editToken (body-only) to editFormResponse.
- app.ts: added three 403 cases INVALID_EDIT_TOKEN / EDITING_DISABLED / EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED to the switch.
- env.ts: RESPONSE_EDIT_SECRET optional(..., 'dev-insecure-response-edit-secret-change-me') + prod console.warn when NODE_ENV===production and the raw env var unset. .env.example documents it under the API section.
- NEW tests: responseEditToken.test.ts (8: round-trip, tampered, bad sig, garbage, truncated, no-separator, no-expiry-check, timingSafeEqual-source-assert) and form.service.test.ts (5: validateSubmission valid/unknown-id/missing-required/MULTI_ENTRY-blank/type-mismatch).

Web changes (apps/web):
- PublicFormPage.tsx: added same-session state responseId/editToken/editWindowExpiresAt/isEditing + a 1s 'now' tick interval (only while a token+window exist). handleSubmit branches: when isEditing+responseId+editToken POST the edit endpoint (keeps same token, returns to confirmation), else POST submit and capture response.id+editToken+computeEditWindowEnd. Helpers computeEditWindowEnd (timed->submittedAt+minutes*60000; until_close->scheduledCloseAt or null), mapEditErrorMessage (403 codes -> design messages), startEditing (clears submitted, resets to section 0; answers stay in memory so the form is prefilled). Confirmation screen shows 'Edit my response' + a window note when a token exists and now<editWindowExpiresAt (or window is null). Submit button label switches to Save changes/Saving when editing.
- FormEditorPage.tsx: added responseEditing/responseEditMinutes state loaded from schema.settings; a Settings-tab control inside the 'Access & Schedule' group (mode select + minutes input shown only when 'timed'); both folded into the shared saveFormSettings PATCH body (alongside theme from FEAT-001).

CROSS-FEATURE NOTES for FEAT-003: ResponseDashboardPage metadata block will now show an 'editedAt' key for edited responses — that is intended (design §2.5). The web FormSchema.settings.responseEditing/responseEditMinutes fields were already present from FEAT-001; I only consumed them. form.service.ts getPublicForm was NOT changed (responseEditing/responseEditMinutes ride through publicSettings automatically, confirmed NOT in the responseNotification/sendConfirmationEmail omit-list).

MANUAL CHECKLIST (design §2.11): NOT run — it needs a live dev server + Postgres + a published test form, which is out of scope for this automated step per design §0 (unit=automated, integration=manual). The security core (token sign/verify) and the answer-validation boundary are fully covered by the automated unit tests above.
